:::caution[Coming in the next release]
These notes are for a release that is not out yet. HotLoop Cascade 1.4.2 is the latest one you can install.
:::

## What this is

1.5.0 lets an owner delete a person. The engine, the file format and every other screen are what 1.4.2 has, and nothing migrates.

## Deleting a person

Before this, the only way to remove an account was to turn it off, and it stayed in the list forever. Now Users has a Delete button beside Turn off, shown to owners for everyone but themselves, and it asks before it does anything. The same call is in the REST API, `DELETE /api/v1/users/{user}`, and in the MCP server as `delete_user`, with the same rule: only an instance owner, never your own account, and never the last owner.

The account, its sessions, passkeys, sign-in identities and API keys go at once, so anything still signed in as that person stops working on its next request. The audit log records who deleted whom, with the email, role and how many sessions and keys went, and its chain still verifies.

Their work stays. Their personal project becomes a shared project named for them with "(removed)" after it, holding every workflow, credential and run it had, and owners and admins can move any of it to another project or give it to someone. The same email can be used to make a new account later, which starts with a project of its own.

Turn off is unchanged and is the right choice when you want the account kept. A person your identity provider removes over SCIM is still switched off and hidden, not deleted.

## Going back

There is no migration, so the previous image runs on the same data. A deleted account does not come back; restore the backup you took before the delete if you need it.

## amd64 only, and why

This release builds amd64 only. Multi-arch ships in its own run, so the release after this one is a single small version bump that builds both. `stable`, `latest`, `1.5` and `1` list the new amd64 image beside the arm64 image they already pointed at.
